speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our long-term relationship will always be bound by the ties of kinship, culture, history and economic interdependence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will, of course, work with the elected government of the day.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A stable and prosperous Malaysia is good for Singapore and for our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have generally enjoyed a positive and constructive relationship with successive Malaysian governments and leaders, and we believe there is still much for us to achieve together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There has been a high tempo of bilateral exchanges since GE14 in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee and I visited Malaysia on 19 May 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We had a good meeting with Prime Minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dr Mahathir updated us on his immediate domestic preoccupations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee emphasised that Singapore wanted to continue cooperating with Malaysia for mutual benefit and that we hoped to keep up our bilateral exchanges, including the annual Leaders’ Retreat.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also invited the new Malaysian leaders to visit Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Several of their Ministers have visited Singapore recently, including Defence Minister Mohamad Sabu who was here for the Shangri-La Dialogue in June 2018, the Communications and Multimedia Minister Gobind Singh Deo for the Smart Nation conference on 7 June 2018, and Housing and Local Government Minister Zuraida Kamaruddin who made a working visit earlier this month.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think it is quite appropriate that Members of this House, citizens of Singapore, would be wondering about these issues, and wondering, as Mr Christopher de Souza has said, how they will affect our bilateral ties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Before I address these specific issues, I want to highlight three fundamental principles of Singapore’s foreign policy that are especially salient for our relationship with Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, upholding international law and respecting the sanctity of international agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a critical principle for a small state like Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our very existence as a sovereign independent state is derived from the Separation Agreement of 1965.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: International agreements, solemnly entered into by countries, are sacrosanct and underpin relationships between sovereign states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They make it possible for countries to co-exist peacefully, build trust and work together for the long-term good of our citizens, regardless of changes of governments or circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The alternative, in which countries can unilaterally revise or abandon terms of agreements, is manifestly a recipe for disaster.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The second principle is that any disputes – here, I must add – in the nature of all relationships, from time to time, disputes will arise, but the principle is that these disputes, if and when they arise, should be resolved in accordance with international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The recent Pedra Branca cases are illustrative of this principle.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The previous Malaysian government had requested the International Court of Justice (ICJ) to revise its original 2008 judgment, and separately to interpret the 2008 ICJ judgment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the Singapore side, we were confident of the correctness of the original 2008 ICJ judgment, and we were confident of our case.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The key point is that both sides followed due legal processes, handled this issue in accordance with international law, and put the matter to rest amicably, as it should be.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The third principle is that we must uphold Singapore's reputation as a credible, trusted and consistent partner, a country that abides fully by our international obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This reputation for Singapore, developed over decades, is crucial for our political and economic space, is crucial for Singapore and Singaporeans, and all the more crucial because we are an international financial centre.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These are three fundamental principles that undergird the way we conduct diplomacy and the way we deal with foreign policy issues as and when they arise.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With these in mind, let me turn to the three current specific bilateral issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Malaysia’s investigations into this issue have intensified following their general election.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members will recall that Singapore has, in fact, been thoroughly investigating 1MDB-related offences that were committed in Singapore since 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So far, we are the only jurisdiction in the world to have done so.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have, in addition, cooperated fully with Malaysia’s official requests for information on 1MDB-related transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We received numerous requests for information from Malaysian authorities between March 2015 and August 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We responded to each and every single request fully.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also proactively provided the Malaysian authorities with additional information on 1MDB-related fund flows on multiple occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Further, since the change of government in Malaysia, over the past few months, Singaporean and Malaysian agencies have met on several occasions on 1MDB matters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, the Malaysian authorities have expressed appreciation to Singapore for our cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We took these investigations and enforcement and regulatory actions not for political calculations, but because it is in our own enlightened national interest to reaffirm and protect Singapore's reputation as a clean, transparent and trusted international financial centre.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do not tolerate the misuse of our financial system as a refuge or conduit for illicit funds.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members have asked several questions on this, and the Minister for Transport, Minister for National Development and Minister for Finance will all address them in detail.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But here, I just want to emphasise that the crux of the issue is the sanctity of international law and agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am heartened to note Malaysian Finance Minister Lim Guan Eng's comments on another project that his Ministry had undertaken with a foreign commercial party.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He said that should the foreign commercial party not adhere to the terms of the agreement within the specified period, his Ministry would be entitled to take certain actions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To quote Mr Lim: "I think we should look at the agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, the point is, Minister Lim Guan Eng, himself, recognises the importance of maintaining the sanctity of agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When Malaysia proposed the HSR in 2013, Singapore studied the proposal carefully, all the more so because of its very large financial commitments.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Subsequently, after due diligence and study, we agreed to pursue the HSR because we were convinced of its benefits to Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We signed the legally binding HSR Bilateral Agreement in 2016 in good faith, after both sides had carefully, painstakingly, meticulously negotiated and agreed to all the provisions, including those pertaining to the implementation of the project, as well as those dealing with the eventuality that the project is terminated.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In recent weeks, however, Members would have seen a range of news reports and quotes from Malaysian leaders about the Malaysian government’s position on HSR.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These include announcements that a “final decision” had been made to terminate the project, subject to discussions with Singapore, and yet other statements that the project has been "postponed" or "deferred".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have sent the Malaysian government a Third Person Note (TPN) requesting clarification of Malaysia’s position.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, the Malaysian government has not yet replied to our TPN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the meantime, Singapore is continuing to incur costs on this project as we continue to meet our obligations under the bilateral agreement, whilst awaiting Malaysia’s clarification.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We look forward to a prompt official response to our TPN from the Malaysian government.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am sure Members of this House will agree with me that the Singapore Government has a duty to safeguard public funds by recovering these costs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This brings me to the third bilateral issue, the price of raw water imported by Singapore from Malaysia under the 1962 Water Agreement, a fundamental agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have stated this publicly many times before, including in this very Chamber, and our position is well-known to everyone, including to Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The 1962 Water Agreement is not an ordinary agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The 1962 Water Agreement was guaranteed by both Malaysia and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This guarantee is in the 1965 Separation Agreement, which, in turn, was registered with the United Nations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Any breach of the	1962	Water Agreement would call into question the Separation Agreement, and Members would remember that the Separation Agreement is the basis for Singapore's very existence as an independent sovereign state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore will fully honour the terms of the 1962 Water Agreement, including the price of water that is stipulated in that agreement, and we expect Malaysia to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members will recall that then-Foreign Minister Prof S Jayakumar and then-Foreign Minister K Shanmugam had stated our position on this issue comprehensively on 25 January 2003 and on 6 March 2014, respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Their key points remain as valid today as when they were first articulated.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As was stated then, the core issue is "not how much we pay, but how any price revision is decided upon".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The core issue is "not how much we pay, but how any price revision is decided upon".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Neither Malaysia nor Singapore can unilaterally change the terms of agreement between our two countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have made this point publicly on multiple occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, Malaysia has previously acknowledged that they themselves chose not to ask for a review in 1987 because they benefited from the pricing arrangement under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This price and, in fact, even the volume, are provided for under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members of this House will know that 50 Malaysian sen per 1,000 gallons is a fraction of the true cost of treating the water.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Hence, in 2002, then-Prime Minister Dr Mahathir, in his first incarnation, said that Malaysia did not ask for a review when it was due as Malaysia knew that any revision would also affect the price of treated water sold by Singapore to Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The then-Johor State Assembly Speaker Zainalabidin Mohd Zain also said, and I quote: "There was no point in   because Johor was dependent on Singapore for its treated water supply, and Singapore would have also increased its price of treated water sold to Johor".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The reason why I am taking pains to recite all these to Members is to make the point that Malaysia took a conscious decision not to review the price when they had the opportunity to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this is why, in fact, even to this date, Johor buys more treated water than it is entitled to, strictly under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These additional supplies of treated water that we have been selling to Johor, at Johor's request, are sold at the same rate stipulated by the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This sale is made on a goodwill basis, and without prejudice to our rights under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition, if in 1987, Malaysia had exercised the right to review the price of water, Singapore would have made quite different investment decisions on developing the Johor River and its water catchment areas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One example of this is the Linggiu Reservoir.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Provided this condition is met, I am confident that our bilateral relations will prosper, for the mutual benefit of citizens of both countries.
